mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over the prior 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings and consumer spending, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2% or greater YoY decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over the prior 6 months signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings growth and compresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when RSAFS falls > 2% YoY (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 1.5% or greater YoY increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) over the prior 6 months signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings expectations and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods when INDPRO rises > 1.5% YoY (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous 0.4 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate and a 2% or greater YoY decline in personal consumption expenditures over the prior 3 months signals a synchronized deterioration in labor and demand conditions, which reduces earnings and growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.4pp AND RSAFS falls > 2% YoY in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when both UNRATE rises > 0.4pp and RSAFS falls > 2% YoY (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.5 percentage point or greater increase in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3% or greater YoY decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with a 1% or greater YoY decline in residential construction starts (HOUST) over the prior 6 months signals a synchronized weakening in household demand and housing activity, which reduces earnings and growth, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls > 3% YoY AND HOUST falls > 1% YoY in 6 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when both RSAFS falls > 3% YoY and HOUST falls > 1% YoY (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point or greater increase in the unemployment rate over the prior 3 months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings and consumer spending, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).
